note: Authored enrichment (agent-researched, cited). Merged into the review doc at render time. Facts are leads to verify, not gospel; sources listed per item.

facts: This is one physical coaster: the 1984 Schwarzkopf triple-looper that toured German fairs as **Dreier Looping** (1984–96), then Sunway Lagoon as **Triple Loop Coaster** (1997–99), Flamingo Land as **Magnum Force** (2000–05), La Feria Chapultepec Mágico as **Montaña Infinitum/Triple Loop/Quimera** (2007–19), and reopened at **Indiana Beach as All American Triple Loop on May 11, 2024**.
The four orphan rows (1997/2005/2007/2022) correspond to different life stages of this same unit, not four rides.
The DB has no Indiana Beach row for it — the coaster is genuinely missing under its current name.
**Batman & Robin: The Chiller** was a dueling Premier LIM shuttle at **Six Flags Great Adventure**, opened 1997, plagued with downtime, last operated 2007 and subsequently removed (track scrapped).
The B&M inverted Batman clones by year: **SFGAm 1992**, SFGAd 1993, **SFMM 1994**, SFSt. Louis 1995, SFOG 1997, **SFOT 1999**, SFNO 2003.

Six Flags Great America ALREADY has a `Batman: The Ride` row (opening 1993 — wrong; the true opening is May 9, **1992**). Recommended: merge this orphan into the existing row and fix the year to 1992.
The orphan's 1992 opening_date is more accurate than the existing row's.

Six Flags Magic Mountain ALREADY has a `Batman: The Ride` row (opening 1997 — wrong; the true opening is March 26, **1994**). Recommended: merge this orphan into the existing row and fix the year to 1994.
Six Flags Over Texas has no Batman: The Ride row yet. Its clone opened **May 26, 1999** and operates. Re-home here creates the row with the correct year.

The 2003 clone opened at **Six Flags New Orleans (April 12, 2003)**; the park closed permanently after Hurricane Katrina (2005). The physical ride was relocated to Six Flags Fiesta Texas where it operates as **Chupacabra** (2008, renamed 2024).

DB has neither an SFNO row nor a Chupacabra row. Cleanest: re-home this orphan to Six Flags New Orleans with status `defunct` (or `relocated`), and treat 'Chupacabra' as a future creation at Fiesta Texas (different name, same physical coaster — an alias candidate).
Only two 4D Free Spin Batmen exist: **Six Flags Fiesta Texas (May 23, 2015)** and **Six Flags Discovery Kingdom (May 25, 2019)**. This 2015 row belongs to Fiesta Texas, which has no such row yet.
The 2019 4D Free Spin Batman belongs to **Six Flags Discovery Kingdom** (opened May 25, 2019), which has no such row yet.

The two `Flashback` rows headed to Magic Mountain (1985/1988) are **one physical ride**: the Intamin Space Diver that operated as **Z-Force @ Six Flags Great America (1985–87)**, then **Z-Force @ Six Flags Over Georgia (1988–91)**, then **Flashback @ Six Flags Magic Mountain (April 25, 1992 – 2003**, scrapped 2007).
Recommended: merge the two orphans into ONE Magic Mountain row with opening year **1992**, status `defunct`; add aliases `Z-Force`.
Same physical ride as ORPH-041 (see context there): merge both into a single Magic Mountain row, opening **1992**, `defunct`.
`Flashback` at **Six Flags Over Texas** was a Vekoma Boomerang (operated 1989–2004; removed). The orphan's 1989 opening year matches.

`Flashback` at **Six Flags New England** is a Vekoma Boomerang (operating) with the relocation chain Star Lake → Kentucky Kingdom (`Vampire`) → SFNE (`Flashback`). The 1990/2000 orphan rows are the same ride double-listed — after re-home, merge into one row.
Same physical ride as ORPH-044 — merge the two after re-homing to Six Flags New England.

The four `American Dreier Looping` rows are life stages of ONE physical coaster — see ORPH-002 context. Recommended composite action: merge all four, re-home the survivor to **Indiana Beach**, rename to **All American Triple Loop**, opening **2024**, status `operating`, aliases: `Dreier Looping`, `Triple Loop Coaster`, `Magnum Force`, `Montaña Infinitum`, `Quimera`.

Do NOT merge: Journey to Atlantis is **three distinct rides** — SeaWorld Orlando (Apr 17, 1998, Mack Water Coaster), SeaWorld San Diego (May 29, 2004), SeaWorld San Antonio (May 11, 2007, Mack SuperSplash). All three parks exist in the DB.

The slug year-suffixes (-2004, -2007) are the sister parks' build years that the source data flattened into the Orlando Location. Recommended: keep the 1998 row at Orlando; re-home the -2004 row to SeaWorld San Diego and the -2007 row to SeaWorld San Antonio.
